[[Deep North]] |Snow-capped hills and forests with frozen rivers, inhabited by [[Moose]], [[Elaking]], and [[Gammeltroll|Gammeltrolls]]. |Northern edge of the world |} == Alternative biomes == Each biome patch has a chance to have modifiers applied to it on world generation, but only a certain distance from the world center. These modifiers can have the following effects: * Affect foliage, like more [[Raspberries]] or only [[Birch]]es in the Meadows, or only stubs in the Black Forest * Generate additional structures, like [[Large Bone]]s in the Swamps, Plains or Mistlands, or more [[Tar Pit]]s in the Plains * Increase the chance for [[creature level|starred]] creatures * Enable the spawning of certain creatures not normally encountered in the biome, such as [[Bat]]s in the Swamp, or increase existing chances for a creature to spawn, like more [[Abomination]]s * Disable the spawning of creatures native to the biome Several modifiers can affect a single area at once. The following biomes can be affected: * [[Meadows#Alternative biomes|Meadows]] has 8 modifiers. * [[Black Forest#Alternative biomes|Black Forests]] have 8 modifiers. * [[Swamp#Alternative biomes|Swamps]] have 5 modifiers. * [[Mountain#Alternative biomes|Mountains]] have 3 modifiers. * [[Plains#Alternative biomes|Plains]] have 5 modifiers. * [[Mistlands#Alternative biomes|Mistlands]] have 6 modifiers. Oceans, the Ashlands and the Deep North do not have any alternative variants. ==Trivia== *The term "biome" comes from the [[wikipedia:biome|ecological concept of the same name]]. *At ''Valheim's'' early access launch in February 2021, five of the planned nine biomes were made available to explore. The other four were accessible, but lacked any meaningful content. ** As of the full release in September 2026, all biomes excluding the Ocean are fully implemented. An Ocean overhaul was ultimately abandoned, with the argument that it only serves the role of a highway between other biomes, which do have meaningful content. * Alternative biomes were introduced in the [[1.0]] release. {{Biomes}} [[de:Biom]] [[ru:Биомы]] [[pt-br:Biomas]] [[uk:Біоми]] [[cs:Biomy]] [[zh-tw:生物群落]] [[Category:Biomes| ]]

[[File:Building screenshot.jpg|thumb|A player building a house]] {{Quote|Raise your own viking mead halls, houses, castles, and more with our powerful construction interface. From knarrs to imposing warships, build legendary vessels to conquer the seas and discover new lands.https://www.valheimgame.com/home/#anchor2}} Valheim features an extensive '''building''' system that can be utilized to design structures to meet the demands of any discriminating warrior. In addition to humble homes and outposts, players also use this building interface to make enormous bases, elaborate works of art, defenses against the [[Creatures]] of Valheim, and unique tools to aid in their survival. Starting out with simple wooden building components, players will eventually gain access to the ability to create stronger structures with various materials, including stone and metal. == Basics == You can build using a [[Hammer]] within the working area of a [[Workbench]]. * Press [1-8] to select the hammer in the hotbar slot * Press [RMB] to open the build menu * Press [Q/E] to switch [[:Category:Building structures|Building Blocks]] category * Press [LMB] to chose [[:Category:Building structures|Building Blocks]], and place it * Press [Middle Mouse Button] to remove [[:Category:Building structures|Building Blocks]] * Scroll the mouse to rotate the [[:Category:Building structures|Building Blocks]] * Hold [Shift] to temporarily disable snapping * Hold [Shift] then [Middle Mouse Button] to select [[:Category:Building structures|Building Blocks]] you are looking at. There are various crafting stations required to be nearby to place certain [[:Category:Building structures|Building Blocks]]. These include the following: * The [[Workbench]], required to place most [[:Category:Building structures|Building Blocks]] you have unlocked from the beginning or early on, and some late [[:Category:Building structures|Building Blocks]]. The Workbench is immediately available and costs 10 ordinary wood to build. * The [[Forge]], required to place most building parts containing metals. The Forge requires [[copper]] to build, and becomes available once the player can mine and refine [[Copper Ore]]. * The [[Stonecutter]], required to place building parts created out of stone, such as the stone walls some abandoned buildings are made out of. The Stonecutter requires [[iron]] to build, and becomes available once the player can collect and refine [[Scrap Iron]]. * The [[Artisan Table]], required to build some crafting stations that as of Patch 0.142.6 are at the end of implemented progression. The Artisan Table requires [[Dragon Tear|Dragon Tears]] to build, which must be obtained by defeating the fourth boss, [[Moder]] the dragon. == Snap building == Most building components can snap to each other. This allows for quick and easy building, but can be temporarily disabled by holding the appropriate key or button. By default, this is L-Shift on mouse and keyboard, and LT+LB on controller. == Structural integrity == {{Main|Building stability}} If there is not enough support, the building pieces will fall down. You may reinforce the building with walls, beams, and poles. When you move the cursor to the building piece, it shows a color range from blue, to green, to red. Blue indicates that the part is as stable as it can be, as dictated by its material. The closer to red on the spectrum, the less stable the part. Attempting to place additional pieces onto one that is fully red may result in the new part breaking off and dropping the resources used to construct it unless the new part has lower stability requirements. The stability of an individual building piece is determined by its material, the stability of the piece it's anchored to and its position relative to it, each additional piece inheriting a fraction of the previous piece's stability. A directly vertical pole of [[Wood]] or [[Stone]] can rise 16 meters off the ground before it cannot support another piece of the same material above it. This is true for [[Wood Wall]], [[Wood Wall Half]], [[Stone Wall 1x1]], [[Stone Wall 2x1]], [[Stone Wall 4x2]], [[Wood Pole 1 m]], [[Wood Pole 2 m]], [[Stone Pillar]]. A directly vertical pole of [[Corewood]] Logs can rise 24 meters off the ground before it cannot support another piece of the same material above it. This is true for [[Log Pole 4 m]] and [[Log Pole 2 m]]. A directly vertical [[Wood Iron Pole]] can rise up to 50 meters off the ground before it cannot support another piece of the same material above it. Trees, including those planted by the player, will effectively function as "the ground" for support purposes, allowing for extremely high construction. [[File:Structure integrity.png|thumb|Found on [https://www.reddit.com/r/valheim/comments/lqsxki/updated_psa_structural_support_details/ Reddit /Valheim], thanks to [https://www.reddit.com/user/ToddGeorgeKelly/ user/ToddGeorgeKelly/]]] In order to keep tall structures stable, the tallest point should be reinforced by supports that create the shortest and most vertical path possible down to the ground. It is worth considering raising the terrain as much as possible below a structure, such that the floor and walls are 100% stable (highlighted in blue when moused over). Boulders are also considered terrain when calculating stability, so parts that intersect them are considered grounded. == Decay == If wooden building sections are not covered during rain, are not linked to a roof, or are submerged in water, they will decay to a maximum of 50% durability and will seem rotting until fixed. When exposed to rain, defensive structures do not rot decay. Stone, black marble, and crystal structures will not decay when wet or submerged. Building the desired structure's roof first, with the appropriate supports and foundation in place, will aid with constructions lasting days or weeks if rain is a worry. == Damage == Player, monster, and creature attacks can all damage structures. Defensive structures will also receive minor damage while causing harm to creatures that come into contact with them. Aggressive creatures are drawn to and hostile toward all light sources (excluding Jack-o-turnips) and crafting stations, and will try to break them if not attacking a player. == Repair == You can repair building parts that seem to be decaying or damaged with a [[Hammer]]. This does not cost any resources, but does consume stamina. The player must be in range of a crafting station that corresponds to the part being repaired, e.g. a [[Workbench]] when repairing a wooden part, or a [[Stonecutter]] for a stone part. == Abandoned buildings == These structures are a type of [[point of interest]] that can be found to naturally occur in the world. The size, layout, and materials these structures are made of can vary greatly as each is generated from random templates. There are different types of abandoned structures such as Abandoned Cabins, Abandoned Towers, Abandoned Farms just to name a few. These abandoned and generated structures can contain things such as chests with items specific to the biome, monsters (usually [[Skeleton]]s), [[:Category:Creature spawner|monster spawner]]s, and [[wikipedia:Vegvísir|Vegvisir]]s to mark the nearest boss altar for that biome. In the Meadows/Black Forest biome, they can also contain naturally spawning [[Beehive]]s, which will drop a [[Queen Bee]] and sometimes [[Honey]] when destroyed. Players should approach abandoned villages with caution since some villages have been reoccupied by [[Draugr]] and [[Draugr Elite]] who will attack the player on sight. These [[Draugr village|Draugr Villages]] can be identified by partial walls of sharp logs and the buzzing of the [[Creature spawner|spawners]] inside several of the buildings as well as a general miasma and the presence of Draugr both inside and outside the structures. They almost always have a large Mead Hall building that cannot be found anywhere else. There may also be a sentry in a tower armed with a bow who will snipe anything that comes near. == Player base and blocking spawning == {{Main|Player base}} Building certain structures considered to be 'player base' will have the following effects in a radius around them: * Prevent [[creatures|creature]] spawning * Prevent items dropped on the ground from despawning after 1 hour (unless submerged) * Enable player base [[events]] to occur For a full list of player base structures, see [[player base]]. == Base building strategies == [[File:Mordheim server - Guild Castle.jpg|thumb|850x850px]] * Building your outposts in close proximity to '''several biome borders''' grants access to varied resources and allows you to observe the territorial in-fighting of different creatures (complete with loot strewn across the terrain), but can also be dangerous. * Many types of '''defenses''' are possible, both in the form of built objects and altered terrain: ** Creatures cannot dig through terrain, making '''"terrain walls" effectively impenetrable''' to them. Thus the perfect defense is built either with a hoe and a pile of rocks, any pickaxe or ideally a combination of the two. Be warned that terrain alterations may cause stutter just as placing objects does (press F2 to check the number of "instances" loaded). ** A hoe can be used to raise terrain while you're standing on it, allowing you to quickly erect a '''pillar''' to stand on and shoot melee enemies below. Beware that you need a workbench nearby to do this. With practice this is possible during combat. ** Most creatures never jump down from ledges (Fenring and Blobs are exceptions). A '''deep pit''' (around 3 "blocks") is also largely safe, and you can shoot enemies coming close to the ledge. Flying creatures may attack from above if you don't build a roof, however. ** Gates can be destroyed, but '''gaps''' the player jumps over when entering or exiting the base cannot. This trick can be inconvenient, however. Also note that you can '''scale steep terrain''' walls by sprinting and jump-spamming, especially when moving towards a crease (corner) for better traction, while most creatures cannot. ** The most '''FPS-efficient method of defense''' is to build on a few terrain pillars. This minimizes terrain alteration "instances" yet allows you to ignore enemies running around outside, especially if the base entrance requires a quick hop to get on. Note that returning terrain to its roughly native height doesn't remove the FPS hit (unless a true "undo terrain changes" tool is added to the game). ** Workbenches (and campfires) '''disallow enemy spawns''' in their radius, making them surprisingly useful defensive tools. You can hide these in the outer perimeter of your walls or in small pits covered with a few floor tiles to make an area safer. Workbenches also stop dropped items from de-spawning over time, however. ** Doors and gates can be used to create a '''toggle-able bridge''' for carts. Another option to defend your bridge is to hang a gate from a support above it and attach the floor piece to the gate with small gaps on the sides, causing the floor to disappear if the gate is destroyed. ** You can place '''gates in the water''' to block enemies, who will be unable to attack the gates, yet allow boats to pass when opened. * The '''"Level Ground"''' option for the hoe uses the terrain height directly underneath you as the target altitude, though if you hold Shift while clicking it'll use the altitude of the terrain you're pointing at instead. Using this knowledge well may save you a lot of stone and work while landscaping as it only expends stamina and hoe durability. * You can also build a '''"gangplank"''' for enemies to walk on, above your pit base, and put a campfire on it so they'll kill themselves, then catch the loot when it drops down. * Combining a moat with a plateau-based outpost is an interesting option. With the ''Grass'' mode, the player can regrow grass on patches of dirt, regrow lily pads on water, create sand on the shoreline and regrow cattails in certain areas around the shore. Use of Cultivator does use stamina, making Hildir's clothing useful for managing large farms. == Availability == Made at a [[Forge]]. It becomes available to craft once the player has obtained [[Bronze]] and [[Corewood]]. == Usage == The Cultivator is a farming tool for tilling soil, planting seeds, and restoring damaged environments. Crops will display a status next to their name when planted until they are fully grown. The ''"Healthy"'' status means the plant is growing. All food crops need cultivated soil. Crops will not grow if any of the three conditions are met: * Wrong biome * Not enough space * Not enough sunlight Some crops can only be planted in certain biome requirements. Planting a crop in the wrong environment will display the ''"Can't grow in this environment"'' status. Most crops require a 1x1 area of free space around them. Other crops, structures, or objects placed within this space will prevent the plant from growing. This is true even for rocks that have been covered by the terrain. Any objects within this free space will cause the "''Needs more room to grow"'' status. Crops require unobstructed view of the sky. Any structures built over a crop will cause the ''"Needs an open sky"'' status, regardless of how high the structure is above the crop. Unique among crops - Vineberry vines need to be 1 away from a flat built wall to climb. It can cross over Window or door openings, but any overhang or break in the wall will stop its growth. Fences and decorative panels count as walls for purpose of trellising. Vineberries needs a greater spacing between plants. Trees are also planted with a Cultivator. '''Silver Ore''' is a raw metal that can be mined from [[Silver Vein]]s found in [[Mountain]] biomes above 120 meters using an [[Iron Pickaxe]] or better. The ore can be smelted into [[Silver]] using a [[Smelter]].

Silver Veins can be found using the [[Wishbone]] obtained from [[Bonemass]].

Alternatively, hitting the ground with the [[Stagbreaker]] or the [[Wooden Sledge]] may reveal underground silver deposits through the "too hard" message that appears when a silver vein is in the damage area of the two-handed club.

Trenching your positions may inadvertently reveal silver veins, provided you are above 120 meters in elevation. Despite the ground appearing frozen, it is no more difficult to dig in the Mountains than in other biomes, so hitting a vein by sheer luck is not out of the question.

* [[Cart]]s may be difficult to use in the Mountains due to the slopes but can be useful to help reduce further trips.
* Silver ore is the heaviest ore of all the ore types.
* Silver Veins cannot be mined by [[Stone Golem]]s or using an [[Antler Pickaxe]].

'''Troll Caves''' are [[Points of Interest (POI)#Dungeons|dungeons]] found in [[Black Forest|Black Forests]]. 

== Description ==
They appear as large rock formations with a large entryway, usually decorated with two or three bone piles.

Troll caves have a 75% chance to have a [[Troll]] inside, and a 33% chance to have one outside the cave. Trolls do not respawn inside the cave, since they are a single-use [[Spawn points|spawn point]], nor do Trolls in the forest return to a cave. Trolls cannot enter or leave, and nothing other than the player can enter the cave, making an empty troll cave a completely safe refuge.  

It is possible to build a [[campfire]] inside a troll cave without being choked by smoke. The only other structures allowed are a [[Cooking Station]], a [[Sitting Log]], and a [[ward]] (the last of which would be useless, since the cave is classified as a dungeon and [[Workbench|workbenches]] cannot be placed there).

'''Crafting''' is the process of converting and combining [[materials]] to create new [[items]]. 

Some basic items can be crafted in the player inventory, but most items require a dedicated crafting station such as a [[Workbench]] or [[Forge]]. Most gear can also be upgraded to a higher quality, increasing its durability and other aspects.

== Crafting mechanics ==
[[File:Crafting-a-Cultivator.jpg|thumb|The crafting interface of a level 2 Forge, showing the recipe of a [[Cultivator]]. The station level is shown within the star in the top right. The craft tab allows crafting new items, whereas the upgrade tab allows upgrading gear currently in the inventory.]]

Crafting an item at a crafting station requires having the appropriate materials in the [[inventory]], as well as an available slot in the inventory for the result.

Gear that has durability can be repaired for free using the hammer icon at the side of the crafting interface at the crafting station where it was crafted (excluding the inventory). Gear that requires a higher station level to be crafed can also only be repaired at a station at that level, upgrading it does not increase this requirement.

Most weapons, tools and armors can be upgraded to higher qualities, often up to 3 times to a quality of 4. Each upgrade level requires a higher station level. Upgrading increases the durability of the item, and also improves its properties: weapons deal higher damage, while armors provide more [[Armor]]. Upgrading costs a considerable amount of resources and can double or triple the crafting cost of a given item over its cost at quality 1.

For example, the [[Troll Leather Tunic]] requires a level 2 Workbench to be crafted. Thus, it cannot be repaired at a level 1 Workbench. Upgrading it to quality 2 requires a level 3 Workbench, to quality 3 a level 4 Workbench, etc. It initially costs 6 [[Troll Hide]] to craft, but upgrading it to quality 4 costs an additional 11 Troll Hide for a total of 17.

The '''Standing Brazier''' is a light source that can be placed on any surface, and must be built within the range of a [[Forge]].

==Usage==
The Standing Brazier has all the same functions as a [[Campfire]] and is a [[Player base|base]] structure.

Standing Braziers are fueled with [[Coal]]. With 1/5 fuel, a Standing Brazier will last for 5 hours and 33 minutes. At maximum capacity, a Standing Brazier should burn for 27 hours and 47 minutes. It can be used for cooking, however, it does not fit easily like a [[Campfire]] does.

The [[Fire Effect]] for the Standing Brazier extends for about 4–5 meters (Measured from the closest the player can stand without setting themselves on fire).

==Notes==
* Destroying the Standing Brazier with a [[Hammer]] will not yield back any [[Coal]] and will only return the 5 [[Bronze]] and 3 [[Fenris Claw]]s used for its construction. All Coal used as fuel and for the initial construction will <u>not</u> be dropped.
* Standing Braziers found in [[Frost Caves]] can be destroyed for Coal and sometimes Bronze.
* Standing Braziers stop working if exposed to rainy weather without a roof.

The '''Eitr Refinery''' is a structure used for processing {{Item Link|Sap}} and {{Item Link|Soft Tissue}} into {{Item Link|Refined Eitr}}.

== Building ==
Eitr Refinery is unlocked once the player has the required materials. A [[Black Metal Axe]] is required to obtain [[Yggdrasil Wood]], and a [[Sap Extractor]] is required to obtain [[Sap]]. The sap extractor requires a [[Dvergr Extractor]] obtained from [[Dvergr Component Crate]]s in Dvergr settlements. [[Infested Mine]]s must also be explored to obtain [[Black Core]]s.

Eitr Refineries can be constructed on flat terrain or on stone floors, but degrade from rain when not under a roof.

== Usage ==
Up to 20 [[Sap]] can be supplied into the funnel at the front of the refinery, and up to 20 [[Soft Tissue]] can be inserted into the grinder at the top. It is possible to climb to the top of the grinder, but constructing stairs makes accessing it easier. The resulting [[Refined Eitr]] is ejected from the tube next to the sap input, opposite the grinder.

The sap:soft tissue ratio is roughly 20:20. Each sap (acting as a fuel) adds 40 seconds, and the operating time on a full fuel tank is 800 seconds. But filling both the Sap and Soft tissue slots to the max will consume 20 Soft tissue and 19 Sap to produce 20 Refined eitr, leaving 1 Sap (probably due to a [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Round-off_error round-off error]).

While processing, small discharges are emitted from the structure, inflicting Lightning and Poison [[Damage]] over time. The eitr dropped on the ground will also emit these discharges, which will eventually damage and destroy structures not immune to elemental damage. Structures immune to elemental damage include [[Cage Wall 2x2|iron]] and [[Dvergr metal wall|copper]] cage pieces, and [[Black Marble]] floor/wall/pillars. Wood and ordinary stone structures will take damage. 

== Notes ==
* As with other [[Mistlands]]-tier structures and items, this can theoretically be obtained before building a [[Wisp Fountain]], but navigation is made difficult by the intense mist.

6000 (gates) | tool tier = 5 |resources = * [[Loot chest#Charred Fortress Charred Chests|Charred chest]] * [[Bell Fragment]] * [[Molten Core]] | resistances = pickaxe only | number = 20 }} '''Charred Fortresses''' are [[Points of interest]] in [[Ashlands]]. They are marked by a beam of green light shooting straight up into the sky, visible from a distance. == Location == Each world has 20 Charred Fortresses. They are always located away from the coasts between the inland lava fields, usually inside the central islands of the Ashlands. == Layout == The fortress consists of a tall, rectangular outer wall with many pillars and spiked bronze defenses. Two opposing outer walls have closed gates in them, leading to the interior area. The interior contains an expanse of ground littered with gravestones, with two [[Effigy of Malice|Effigies of Malice]] in the corners and two stone ramps leading up to the parapets atop the exterior walls. In the very center of the fortress interior is a tall tower, capped with more spiked defenses, which has one gate leading inside. The walls (of the exterior and of the interior tower), the pillars, gates and spiked defenses can all be destroyed, but only by [[Damage#Pickaxe|Pickaxe damage of tool tier 5 or higher]] - i.e. a [[Battering Ram]] or a [[Catapult]] with [[Explosive Payload]]s. The pillars have negligible (1) health but the walls (1500), spikes (1500) and especially the gates (6000) have much higher health. The exterior walls are three layers thick, whereas the interior tower walls are only one layer thick. The fortress initially spawns some creatures, independently to the Effigies of Malice, they do not respawn if killed: * Up to 3 [[Charred Warlock]]s (100% chance for the one on top of the tower and 60% chance to spawn for the other). * Up to 5 [[Charred Marksman|Charred Marksmen]] (100% chance for the one on top of the tower and 60% chance to spawn for the other). * Up to 4 [[Skugg]]s (80% chance for each corner of the fortress to have one). == Loot == Inside the central tower can be found: * A Bell Altar, drops 2 to 4 {{Item link|Bell Fragment}}s when destroyed. * A [[Loot chest#Charred Fortress Charred Chests|Charred chest]]. * A [[Vegvisir|Fader Vegvisir]] with a 50% chance to spawn. * 2 [[Molten Core]]s. Other places inside the Fortress: * The interior court can have up to 8 [[Molten Core]]s, with a 5% chance each to spawn. * Up to 3 Charred chests can spawn along the solid walls of the tower (clockwise from the tower entrance: 100%, 13% and 50% chances to spawn). * [[Skugg]] drop {{item link|Charred Cogwheel}}s which allow the player to make a [[Catapult]]. * The bronze spike strips can be destroyed to drop 2-5 [[Scrap Bronze]] each. As each Charred Fortress contains exactly 78 spike strips, one fortress will yield an average of 273 scrap bronze. The content of Charred Chests is: {{Chest|Charred Chest}} == Notes == * The exterior walls (3 layers x 1500 health = 4500 total) are easier to break through than the gates (6000 health). The tower walls (1500 health) are easier still, but be careful not to accidentally destroy any loot (see below). * The Charred chests and the Bell fragment altar are destroyable; while the chests have 200 health and are resistant to most types of damage (except for [[Damage#Lightning|Lightning]], [[Damage#Poison|Poison]] and [[Damage#Spirit|Spirit]]), the altar is extremely fragile - having only 10 health and no damage resistances. * The presence of the Bell fragment altar is indicated by a huge vertical beacon of light, which can be seen at a distance. This beacon can help identify the location of intact fortresses from afar. ** Destroying the altar also removes the beacon. * The eastern and western smaller islands usually generate with no fortress, thus it is best to first land directly south of spawn. * Some segments of the walls can be mined with any pickaxe. This might be due to a bug. == Tips == * A simple strategy to conquer Charred Fortresses is to first master one Charred Fortress, obtain a [[Bloodstone]], and then craft the [[Trollstav]]. Now, the player can easily approach a Charred Fortress and summon [[Summoned Troll]]s from the outside, which will handle the fortress without any issues. Finally, kill the Troll and enjoy the loot! * It is easier to build a wooden ladder to get on top of the wall rather than using a [[Battering Ram]] to destroy the gates/walls. And, if you are lucky with the world generation, you could use one of the naturally spawning giant rocks to get inside too. Once on top of the walls, simply run circles in the walls and slowly kill enemies and destroy the [[Effigy of Malice|spawners]], if you get overwhelmed just jump off outside (be careful if there is lava). * You can destroy the [[Skugg|skuggs]] from outside the fortress with the bow/crossbow or magic, and from a high enough place you can also destroy the [[Effigy of Malice|spawners]] too. * If you conquered the fortress and didn´t destroy the walls/gates to get inside, the fortress is now a perfect place to build a mini base, thanks to the indestructible walls. Only the flying [[Fallen Valkyrie|valkyries]] and [[Volture|Voltures]] can get inside. * There are two ways to get inside the central tower without a [[Battering Ram]]. First is to make a hole on the ground with a pickaxe and simply pass below the wall of the tower (this may not work if you hit the limit on how low the ground can go). Second is to get on top of the tower and get inside through the hole between the spikes, to get out you will need to either portal out or build yourself ladders/platforms to pass through the hole between the spikes again. == Gallery == Charred fortress tower interior.png|The inside of a Charred Fortress tower. The '''Grappling Hook''' is a [[Mistlands]]-tier tool used for traversal.

== Availability ==
All ingredients for a Grappling Hook can be obtained in the Mistlands. Particularly, the {{Item link|Hook}} can be found in [[Infested Mine]]s, ruined [[Dvergr Guard Tower]]s and on the top of [[Rock Spire]]s.

It cannot be upgraded.

== Recipe ==
The Grappling Hook is crafted at a level 1 [[Black Forge]] with:
* {{Item link|Yggdrasil Wood|10}}
* {{Item link|Refined Eitr|10}}
* {{Item link|Mandible|4}}
* {{Item link|Hook|1}}

== Usage ==
The hook can be shot in a limited range (just over 40 meters), and then retracted. It is particularly useful for traversing the craggy Mistlands terrain.

Both the primary and the secondary attack fire a hook projectile, and each costs 15 [[Stamina]].

Caution should be taken to avoid lethal fall damage; a {{Item link|Feather Cape}} can be worn to prevent it.
